# @aponiajs/mcp

> A Model Context Protocol endpoint for an Aponia application, mounted from the official `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` server. The package contributes a module registration, a validated endpoint policy, a request gate, and stateful session cleanup; every protocol frame is the SDK's.

## What this package exports

- `McpModule` — `McpModule.register(options)` returns the `DynamicModule` an application's `imports` accepts.
- `McpConfiguration` — the value a `defineConfiguration` token validates: `path`, `allowedOrigins`, and `allowUnauthenticated`.
- `McpModuleOptions` — `configuration`, `imports`, `inject`, `useFactory`, `authorize`, `sessions`, `jsonResponse`, `source`, and `key`.
- `McpServerFactory` — `() => McpServer`, called once per request in stateless mode and once per session in stateful mode.
- `McpAuthorize` — `(request) => boolean | Promise<boolean>`; `false` or a throw is a `401`.

## Where the behavior lives

- [McpModule](https://github.com/aponiajs/aponiajs/blob/release/alpha/packages/mcp/src/module/mcp-module.ts): the registration, the configuration provider, and the session registry provider.
- [readMcpPolicy](https://github.com/aponiajs/aponiajs/blob/release/alpha/packages/mcp/src/policy/mcp-policy.ts): the boot guard, the Origin gate, the `authorize` decision, and the preflight answer.
- [McpSessionRegistry](https://github.com/aponiajs/aponiajs/blob/release/alpha/packages/mcp/src/session/mcp-session-registry.ts): the stateful sessions one boot owns and their shutdown.

## Use it

```ts
const mcp = McpModule.register({
  configuration: McpConfig,
  inject: [UsersService],
  useFactory: (users) => () => buildServer(users),
  authorize: (request) => verifyToken(request),
});
```
